_about: Connectors the bench needs that iFixit's chip-ID boxes do not cover (they box chips, not sockets). Coordinates are fractions of the board itself, not of the photo. Read by hand from iFixit's teardown photos; each entry says which one. Everything else on these boards is generated from the chip-ID boxes.

mbneo.note: The MacBook Neo's logic board, drawn from iFixit's chip-ID photo (and 2.4 times taller than life, so the parts are big enough to work on). A long strip along the hinge, like every modern MacBook: the A18 Pro with its memory stacked on top in the middle, soldered storage beside it. What is different is around it: the USB-C ports are their own little board on a press connector, and the battery connector sits front and centre under a two-screw cover.

connectors.label: Battery connector (under a two-screw cover)
connectors.from: Article: 'The battery connector is front and center'; MacBook_Neo_77 shows the press-connector pads on the battery-facing edge.

connectors.label: USB-C port module connector
connectors.from: iFixit's chip-ID boxes put both USB-C port controllers (SN2012027) and the USB hub at this end, beside the vertical press connector seen in MacBook_Neo_77. (MacBook_Neo_71 shows the board flipped, which is why the ports appear at the other end there.)

connectors.label: Display connector
connectors.from: MacBook_Neo_77: the vertical flex connector at the end away from the ports.
